title: Middleton optician invests £34,000 in new dry-eye services
excerpt: Specsavers in Middleton Shopping Centre has invested £34,000 in equipment for new dry-eye procedures, including IPL, low-level light therapy and an eyelid-cleaning service.
body:
A Middleton optician has invested £34,000 in new equipment aimed at helping customers experiencing dry, sore and irritated eyes.

Specsavers in Middleton Shopping Centre has introduced Intense Pulsed Light, known as IPL, and Low-Level Light Therapy, or LLLT, as part of an expanded dry-eye service at the locally owned and run store.

The procedures are designed to support the function of glands around the eyelids which help produce the oily layer of tears and prevent moisture from evaporating too quickly.

According to the store, IPL uses controlled pulses of light to gently warm the area around the eyelid glands, while LLLT uses low-level light. The business says the treatments may help improve gland function and tear quality for some people with dry-eye symptoms.

The Middleton branch has also introduced a service called ZEST, a non-invasive eyelid-cleaning procedure which typically takes around 10 to 20 minutes.

The procedure uses an okra-based gel and a specialised swab to clean the eyelids and lashes, removing debris and build-up around the oil glands.

Dry-eye symptoms can include sore, itchy or irritated eyes, redness, excessive watering and blurred vision. The condition can have a number of causes and contributing factors, including ageing, hormonal changes, prolonged screen use, heating and air conditioning.

Krupal Sheth, optometrist director at Specsavers Middleton, said people should not assume persistent dry-eye symptoms are simply something they have to tolerate.

He said: ‘Many people assume dry eyes are simply something they must live with, but untreated dry eye can significantly impact quality of life, comfort and even vision. Symptoms can sometimes worsen over time if the underlying cause is not addressed properly.’

Mr Sheth said anyone experiencing symptoms should have their eyes assessed by an optometrist, particularly because dry-eye symptoms can sometimes overlap with other eye conditions.

He added: ‘We’re delighted to be able to provide these new procedures, which will greatly benefit the people of Middleton.’

The store says the new services may be suitable for some people who experience dry, itchy or irritated eyes while wearing contact lenses, or who regularly rely on lubricating eye drops. Suitability will depend on an individual assessment.

Anyone with persistent eye pain, sudden changes in vision, severe redness, light sensitivity or an eye injury should seek appropriate medical or urgent eye-care advice rather than relying on a routine dry-eye appointment.

Specsavers Middleton can be contacted on 0161 654 0440. Appointments and further information are also available through the store’s page on the Specsavers website.
